source.basis: Operator spec page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
CyrusOne Sterling's three-building campus provides 44 MW of IT capacity, 2.7% of Virginia's published 1,603 MW, ranking 12th among the 25 facilities that disclose power figures.

The campus spans 420,000 square feet across NVA1, NVA2, and NVA3. At a typical AI training density of 40 kW per rack, 44 MW implies roughly 1,100 racks available for compute. Virginia has 330 mapped data center facilities, but only 25 publish power specifications, so this campus is a mid-tier contributor to the state's disclosed load.

The certifications cover financial services, healthcare, federal compliance, information security, and physical plant standards. They signal readiness for regulated workloads but do not show whether any capacity is allocated to AI. The suitability score of 70 rests on published IT capacity and operator type, with no announced expansion recorded.

Tenant mix and actual power utilization are unpublished. Whether Sterling matters to AI scaling depends on those factors, not on its certification list or its rank among disclosed facilities.

suitability.basis: weighted mean of the published inputs named here, scaled to 100; formula on the methodology page
